issues.display_title: Issue #763: feat(editor): Closed room type — cleanup, placement blocking, colour persistence and undo (#735)
issues.main_description_html:
Source PRD: #735 · Design: #741 · Design branch: design/closed-room-type

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The design branch shipped the Closed room's looks — type radio, colour and logo controls, shell and wall paint, on-map logo. It did not ship its behaviour. src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/closedRoom.ts says so in its own header: closedRoomConflicts (R12–R16 cleanup) and blockingClosedArea (R17–R20 placement blocking) were "finished and tested but deliberately NOT wired up — the functional pack owns their call sites". Zero call sites outside their unit tests.

Scope

  • R12–R16, R21 — converting a room to Closed sweeps the points, shapes and interior doors/windows strictly inside it, under one undo snapshot, with a count-accurate toast. Boundary openings stay (openings are placed by midpoint). Nested rooms are cut out via ctx.rooms[i].holes, so a Closed concourse does not swallow the shop island standing in it.
  • R17–R20 — the point/shape tools guard by the click, addOpeningOnWall by the projected opening midpoint, pasteOpening per record.
  • Persistence — modelToLevel rebuilt every AreaLayer from a field whitelist, so the new color died on the first 2D edit and the 2 s autosave made it permanent. It now spreads from the previous area.
  • Undo — area type and colour ride the engine snapshot as model.areaMeta (the roomHeights pattern); points/safety join the snapshot so the sweep is reversible; a store-side write that touches either becomes its own undo step first, so a pano import or a pin drag is not resurrected by an unrelated Ctrl+Z.
  • Colour picker is a begin/commit gesture — one snapshot per gesture instead of one per tick, which used to flush the map tab's 50-entry history and fire a collab edit per tick.

Acceptance

PRD §10 checklist, 24 lines. 22 pass. Two are PM scope calls, not code:

  • Line 9 "only Closed rooms show a logo above the room" — the Map tab renders a logo for any Information with labelType: "logo", reachable from the Information modal's Label tab. Gating it on the Closed type deletes a shipped feature.
  • Line 18 "cannot add points inside" — the bulk pano import (editorSlice.addPoint) is deliberately exempt; blocking half an import mid-flight is worse than the clutter.

Known, out of scope — needs its own task if wanted

  • After Load floorplan .txt every room is seeded with no type, so a type positionally inherited from the replaced plan is cleared at load. infoId still survives positionally.
  • Collab cannot express "type/colour cleared": sync.ts falls back to the peer's stale value, so an undo does not reach peers and their autosave writes it back. Needs an absent-vs-cleared wire signal.
  • Access markers are still absent from the engine snapshot while deleteSelected removes them under a pushUndo.

Status

Branch feature/735-closed-room-type (merge of design/closed-room-type + the functional pack). pnpm exec tsc --noEmit, pnpm lint and pnpm test (165 files / 1488 tests) green. Not pushed yet.

RESULT

PR #765 → development. Branch feature/735-closed-room-type, commit 6badb0d on top of the design/closed-room-type merge. 27 files, +1486 / −125.

Wired up: conversion sweep (R12–R16, R21) as one undoable engine command, hole-aware so a Closed concourse leaves a nested shop alone; placement blocking (R17–R20) at all three creation paths — point/shape tools by the click, addOpeningOnWall and pasteOpening by the opening midpoint, which is what keeps boundary openings legal.

Made to survive: modelToLevel spreads from the previous area instead of a field whitelist, so color (and anything added later) stops dying on the next 2D edit; type and colour ride the engine undo snapshot as model.areaMeta; points/safety join the snapshot so the sweep is reversible, with a store-side write becoming its own undo step first so a pano import is not resurrected by an unrelated Ctrl+Z; the colour picker became a begin/commit gesture — one snapshot and one store write per gesture instead of per tick.

Also: the on-map logo box no longer collapses on a rotated floor and suppresses itself on a room too small for it, matching 2D; the logo Remove button no longer clears a shared Information record's labelType.

Acceptance: PRD §10 — 22 of 24 pass. Lines 9 and 18 are the PM scope calls named in the description, not defects.

Verification: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit, pnpm lint, pnpm test → 165 files / 1488 passed, 3 skipped.

Carried into the PR description for the reviewer: the Load floorplan .txt type-clearing behaviour change, the collab absent-vs-cleared gap, access markers still missing from the snapshot, and the PERSIST_MAX headroom.

issues.display_title: Issue #764: feat(events): Event Highlights — persistence, cross-floor Place button and Place tab (#740)
issues.main_description_html:
Source PRD: #740 · Design: #742 · Design branch: design/event-highlights

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The design branch delivered Event Highlights end to end — Highlights sidebar section, Event modal (Basic / Media / Date / Place), visitor Event panel, related-events strip in Information cards, derived status against the building clock. It merged into development clean. What it did not deliver is persistence, plus three cross-floor defects.

Scope

  • Persistence (blocker, needs the BE task below) — the branch claims "events ride the existing project snapshot, no new API". The FE half is correct (wizardState.ts emits and reads eventRecords), but POST /v1/floorplan whitelists jsonData field by field and has no eventRecords case, no column, and no field in the response. Every Event saved to localStorage only, returned 200, and died on reload; preview, /v/{key} and /embed/{key} never saw one.
  • R38 cross-floor Place button — PreviewOverlay switched the floor and set the selection in the same batch, so the per-level reset cleared the selection it had just made: the floor moved, nothing was selected, no Information card opened. selectOnLevel now claims the new level on prevActiveRef first; both cross-floor handlers route through it.
  • Editor map tab — the floor-switch effect cleared selectedFeatureIds wholesale. It now filters to the ids the arriving level actually holds (walls and areas included, not only marker anchors) and reads the store imperatively so a canvas edit no longer wipes the selection.
  • Place tab — used a local levelId + objectId matcher, so an object whose Information link was swapped still showed the stale place as selected while the sidebar correctly showed none. It now calls the shared resolvePlace.

Depends on

Backend: event_records column + whitelist + response + duplicate repoint — see the BE task on Project #112. Deploy order: the BE change must land first or with this, or Events still vanish on reload.

Status

Branch feature/740-event-highlights. pnpm exec tsc --noEmit, pnpm lint and pnpm test (166 files / 1416 tests) green. Not pushed yet.

RESULT

PR #766 → development. Branch feature/740-event-highlights, commits 7b8e3fe and 54e8d48 on top of the design/event-highlights merge (clean, zero conflicts).

Persistence: the blocker was entirely backend — POST /v1/floorplan whitelists jsonData field by field and had no eventRecords case, so Events returned 200 and vanished. Fixed in GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#157. That must merge first or with this, migration included. No frontend change was needed; wizardState.ts was already correct.

R38 cross-floor Place button: PreviewOverlay and Editor3DMapView both switched floor and set selection in one batch, so the per-level reset ate the selection it had just made. selectOnLevel claims the new level on prevActiveRef first; the editor effect filters the selection to ids the arriving level holds (walls and areas included) instead of clearing it.

Place tab: now uses the shared resolvePlace, so a place whose Information link was swapped reads as "no place" in the modal exactly as it already did in the sidebar.

Not a bug: the reported cross-building jump failure did not reproduce — setActiveLevelId already re-points selectedBuildingId (#547). A regression test pins it instead of a code change.

Verification: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit, pnpm lint, pnpm test → 166 files / 1416 passed, 3 skipped.

issues.display_title: Issue #767: fix(editor): the Closed room refusal never names a detected room, only a renamed one
issues.main_description_html:
Found while recording the #735 demo against the real app — not from reading the code. It does not affect a PR that already merged.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

Try to place a point or a shape inside a Closed room and the refusal reads:

this room is a closed room — points and shapes can't go inside it

It never says which room, on any imported or wall-detected plan. It only names one after a human has renamed it by hand.

Why

src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:117 and src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interaction-tools.ts:37 both build the message as:

`${blocked.name || "this room"} is a closed room — …`

blocked is a Room off ctx.rooms, and a wall-detected room ships with name: "". The "Area 1" the object panel shows is not room.name — it is synthesised at display time (src/components/editor/panel/EngineRoomList.tsx:23, r.name || `Area ${r.i + 1}`, the same convention as rowName in src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:106). The engine never sees it.

Measured on the demo project: before the rename the banner said "this room is a closed room — …"; after renaming it to "Unit 12" the same click said "Unit 12 is a closed room — …".

Fix

Give the engine the one label the UI already agreed on rather than inventing a second one. closedRoomAt (hittest.ts) returns the Room and the guard knows its index, so name || `Area ${i + 1}` at both call sites is the whole change. Worth extracting so the two guards and the panel cannot drift.

Check

Extend src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/click-cycle.test.ts — its Closed-room guard block already drives onPointerDown and reads the blocked status. Assert an UNNAMED closed room's refusal still identifies it.

issues.display_title: Issue #768: fix(editor): Ctrl+Z does nothing while the Closed room colour swatch holds focus
issues.main_description_html:
Found while recording the #735 demo against the real app, and isolated with a dedicated headless run.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

Pick a colour for a Closed room, then press Ctrl+Z. Nothing. Keyboard undo stays inert until you click away from the swatch. The toolbar Undo button works the whole time.

Measured, on development:

converted:                       48 objects, Closed
focus after picking a colour:    INPUT[color]  "Closed room color"
ctrl+z with the swatch focused → 48  Closed     (nothing happened)
focus after clicking the canvas: BODY
ctrl+z                         → 48             (undid the colour)
ctrl+z                         → 49             (undid the conversion + restored the sweep)

So the undo steps are all correctly on the stack — they are simply unreachable from the keyboard while the picker holds focus.

Why it is worth a ticket

PRD docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-19-closed-room-type/prd.md §4 says changing a Closed room's colour must be reversible "via existing undo behavior". That is true by button and false by keyboard, and the keyboard is what the R21 toast tells the user to press.

Reading the code suggests it should work: the engine's handler is on window (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/index.ts:91), so a keydown anywhere should reach it. It does not, which is why this needs a look rather than a guess. Prime suspect is the native <input type="color"> swallowing the event before it bubbles.

Not a regression from #765

The begin/commit colour gesture landed in #765 and is doing its job — the snapshot exists and the button reverses it. This is about the event never arriving.

Where to start

  • The swatch: src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/SelectionToolbars.tsx (the Closed-room colour input, its onPointerDown / onBlur pair).
  • The handler: keyDown wired at src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/index.ts:91, Ctrl+Z branch in src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts.
  • Check whether the same hole exists on the other colour and slider controls in that toolbar (shape colour, room height, wall width) — if it does, fix it once for all of them rather than per control.

issues.display_title: Issue #769: fix(editor): an Information-linked object stops being an eligible Event place after a save/reload
issues.main_description_html:
Found while recording the #740 demo. Outside #740's scope, and reproduced on development (HEAD 3dc3705) across three separate reads of the same project, so it is data behaviour, not a deploy.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

On the demo project the Event modal's Place dropdown listed five eligible places:

meeting kelapa · Floor 1
baru          · Floor 1
atap kelapa   · Floor 2
tester        · Floor 1
developer room· Floor 1

After one save → reload cycle, "baru" was gone — and it is still gone on a fresh read. The Information counter is unchanged at 38, so the Information record survived. The object carrying the link to it stopped being an eligible place, permanently.

Why it matters beyond Events

eventPlaceOptions (src/lib/events/places.ts) lists areas and shapes that carry an infoId, minus hallway / open-to-below / wall. So either the object lost its infoId or it stopped being an area. If an object can silently lose its Information link across a save/hydrate round trip, the blast radius is much wider than the Place dropdown — Information markers, search and the visitor cards all key off the same link.

Lead, not a diagnosis

hydratePersistedState runs migrateLegacyAccess on load (src/lib/editor/access.ts), which converts legacy stair/lift areas into accessPoints. An accessPoint is not an eligible place — and if the conversion drops the area's infoId on the way, the link is gone for good, because the migration is one-way and the next save persists the migrated shape.

That fits the symptom (one-way, survives reload, record intact) but was not chased: confirming it means driving the 2D editor and mutating the demo project further.

Suggested first step

Take a project snapshot before and after one hydrate cycle and diff layout.areas[].infoId against accessPoints[]. If a migrated area's infoId is not carried onto the access point, that is the bug and the fix is to carry it — plus a decision on whether an access point should be an eligible Event place at all.

Check

src/lib/editor/__tests__/ already covers migrateLegacyAccess. A legacy lift area with an infoId going through the migration and keeping its link is the case to add.

issues.display_title: Issue #725: Any geometry write moves a rotated or scaled floor on the map, not just the vertex drag
issues.main_description_html:
#724 fixed this for the Map-mode wall-vertex drag. The same defect exists for every other geometry write, and it should be closed the same way before someone hits it from the 2D editor.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The general problem

All three map placement frames pivot on a centre derived from live geometry:

Frame Pivot Source
Project canvas bounding-box centre makePixelRotator, geojson-utils.ts:119-122
Building its member levels' bbox centres makeBuildingRecordTransform → buildingBBoxCenter:204
Level the level's own bbox centre makeLevelLocalTransform:180

So any edit that changes a bounding box re-pivots the placement, and a floor that has been rotated or scaled on the map slides. Pure translation is immune — the pivot cancels.

The pivots are deliberate: makePixelRotator's comment explains that a persisted coordSpace centre can sit away from the model, which would make rotation orbit instead of spin. The fix is not to change the pivots but to compensate the offset when they move, which preserveMapPlacement (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts) now does.

What is still unguarded

Every write that changes wall, area or shape geometry on a placed floor. The obvious one is the 2D editor: draw or drag anything there, switch to Map, and a rotated floor will have moved. Others to check — this list is a starting point, not a survey:

  • the floorplan engine's change callback in FloorplanEditor.tsx, which writes setCanvasData on every committed edit
  • replaceLevelContent / fillMissingLevels (lib/editor/levels.ts)
  • the AI scan writing a level back in StepGenerate.tsx and useAddLevel.ts
  • the Mappedin merge (mergeImportIntoProject)
  • deleteLevel and the buildings slice, where removing a level moves a building's centre

Scope

  1. Survey every setCanvasData caller that changes geometry, and say for each whether the floor can be placed at that point in the flow — a wizard project has no placement yet, so most wizard writes are safe by construction.
  2. Route the ones that can through preserveMapPlacement(before, after, levelId).
  3. Decide whether this belongs at the store boundary instead — setCanvasData could compare the incoming canvas against the current one and compensate centrally, which would close the whole class at once. Weigh that against the cost of running a bbox diff on every write, including the 2s autosave path.

Option 3 is probably the right answer and worth costing properly before touching call sites one by one.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editing geometry in the 2D editor leaves a rotated or scaled floor exactly where it was on the map.
  • Deleting a level does not move the remaining floors of that building.
  • Whichever approach is taken, there is one test per placement frame proving an untouched point does not move.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #250: Share meta card (Open Graph / Twitter) for /v/{key}
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: @alfarez21

Description

Split out of #245. /v/{key} is a client component, so add a server generateMetadata producing:

  • title: {Project Name}
  • description: Explore in interactive 3D and find your way around before you even arrive.
  • og:url / canonical: resolved from metadataBase — already set in src/app/layout.tsx from SITE_URL (src/lib/seo.ts)
  • og:image: rendered map + 3D building of the project

Scope (validated against the code on 21 Aug 2026)

1. src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx — server component with generateMetadata({ params })

  • Reads the live blob with getLiveFloorplanAction(key) (src/actions/projects.ts:259). The project name is already in that blob — PersistedState.projectName (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:32), written by buildPersistedState on every save — so no BE change is needed for the title. Fall back to MapThru when it is absent (projects saved before the field existed).
  • title: { absolute: projectName } so the card shows the bare project name; the root layout's template: "%s · MapThru" would otherwise append the suffix.
  • openGraph + twitter (card: "summary_large_image") blocks follow the existing landing-page pattern in src/app/page.tsx.
  • Unknown / unpublished key (live fetch returns null) → generic metadata, no throw.

2. src/app/api/og/[key]/route.ts — the og:image, Playwright running in-process in Next

  • Cache hit → stream /home/config/og/{key}.png.
  • Miss → screenshot localhost:3003/v/{key}?og=1 at 1200×630, write the cache file, stream it.
  • ?og=1 on the viewer hides the information detail card and controls, and the shot waits for the MapLibre idle event so the 3D buildings are painted.
  • Invalidation: delete {key}.png when the project is published.

3. Guards — mandatory because the browser runs inside the Next server

  • One persistent browser instance + a queue with concurrency 1.
  • 15s timeout, close in finally.
  • pm2 fork mode, not cluster.
  • serverExternalPackages: ["playwright"] in next.config.
  • Deploy step installs chromium on the prod VM.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Sharing a /v/{key} link shows the card: map+3D thumbnail, project name as title, the fixed description, link map-thru.com
  • Metadata is present in the server-rendered HTML (crawler sees it with JS disabled)
  • An unknown or unpublished key renders a generic card instead of 500
  • A second scrape of the same key serves the cached PNG without re-screenshotting
  • Publishing a project drops its cached PNG

Why not the alternatives

  • thumbnail_url from the BE — firstThumbnailURL returns the raw uploaded 2D floorplan image of the first level, not a render; fails the AC.
  • opengraph-image.tsx + ImageResponse — cannot render MapLibre / WebGL.
  • Separate screenshot service or mbgl-renderer next to tileserver-gl — new infra. Keep it as the upgrade path if the in-process browser OOMs or traffic grows: move the route to its own pm2 service on :3004.

The 3D buildings in the live viewer are MapLibre fill-extrusion (src/lib/map/layer-definitions.ts), not three.js, so a headless screenshot reproduces them.

Dependencies

  • #245 — route exists, done.
  • No BE task. An earlier version of this issue asked the BE for name and an og image URL on the public live response; the name already rides in the live blob, and the image is rendered on the FE.

Updated 21 Aug 2026: the three blocking open questions are resolved — image source = Playwright in-process with a disk cache (option C/D hybrid, FE-only), title = bare project name via title: { absolute }, project name = read from the live blob. The 16 Jul correction below still stands: the repo does have a complete OG setup on the landing page, only the per-project image was missing.

Correction (16 Jul 2026): an earlier version of this issue claimed the repo had
"zero OG implementation today — no openGraph block, no opengraph-image, no
generateMetadata". That was wrong: it came from a search run against a stale working
tree, before the branch was cut from development. The repo has a complete openGraph
setup on the landing page (src/app/layout.tsx metadataBase + title template,
src/app/page.tsx openGraph/twitter/JSON-LD); only the per-project rendered
map+3D image was ever missing.
